activity_context.topic_title: Laplace Transforms of Piecewise Continuous Functions

feedback.problem:
Use the definition of Laplace transforms to calculate $F(s)=L{f(t)},$ where $f(t)$ is given by 

$$
f(t)={\begin{aligned}-1,\, & x\le 4 \\ 1\, & x>4\end{aligned}
$$

$\,F(s)=L{f(t)}=$ {{field-1}},
valid for {{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We apply the definition of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =F(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }f(t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

So, for the piecewise function 

$$
f(t)={\begin{aligned}-1,\, & x\le 4 \\ 1\, & x>4\end{aligned}
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }f(t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(-1)\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{4}^{\infty }1\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{4}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the improper integral diverges if $s\le 0.$

For $s>0,$ we calculate our Laplace transform as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & =-{\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{4}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{s}{[{e}^{-st}]}_{0}^{4}+{\int }_{4}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-4s}}{s}-\frac{1}{s}+{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{4}^{a}{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-4s}}{s}-\frac{1}{s}+{lim}_{a\to \infty }{(-\frac{{e}^{-st}}{s})|}_{4}^{a} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-4s}}{s}-\frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{s}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }({e}^{-sa}-{e}^{-4s}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-4s}}{s}-\frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{s}(0-{e}^{-4s}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-4s}}{s}-\frac{1}{s}+\frac{{e}^{-4s}}{s} \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{-4s}}{s}-\frac{1}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>0.$
